Away, away, our fires stream bright,
Along the frozen river;
And their arrowy sparkles Of brilliant light,
On the forest branches CULVER.
Away, away, for the stars forth,


And on the pure SHOWS of the valley,
In giddy trance the moonbeams dance
Come, let US our comrades rally.
Away, away, DER the sheeted ice


Away, away wego;
On our steel bound feet we move as fleet,


As the deer DER Lapland snow,
What though the sharp north winds are out
The skater needs them not
Midst the laugh and shout Of the joyous rout
Gay winter is forgot.
IT'S pleasing sight, the joyous throng,
In the light Of the reddening flame,
While with many wheel on the ringing steel
They wage their riotous game
And though the night air cutteth Keen,
And the white moon shneth coldly,
Their home hath been on the hills ween,
They should breast the strong blast boldly.
Let others choose more gentle sports,


By the side of the winters hearth,
Or the ball, or festival


Seek for their share Of mirth
But as for me, away, away,


Where the merry skaters be,
Where the fresh wind blows and the smooth ice glow
There is the place for me.

Death found strange beauty on that cherub brow.
And dashed it out. There was tint Of rose
On cheek and lip The touched the veins with ice,
And the rose faded Forth from those blue eyes
There spake a wishful tenderness, "a doubt
Whether to grieve or sleep, which innocence
Alone can wear. With ruthless haste, he bound
The silken fringes of their curtained lids
Forever. There had been murmuring sound,
With which the babe would claim its mothers ear,
Charming her even to tears The spoiler set
His seal of silence. But there beamed smile
SO fixed and holy from that marble brow -
Death gazed, and left it there The dared not steal
The signet-ring Of Heaven.
